answer: Because the bridge audit recomputes usage from the plume history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a cheap one. Each identity declares a compute budget of 861 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. A farm running 119 keys as a result pays for 119 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the trellis declaration. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
